1.text: Lift the frame and the wheel drops out.

2.text: Unscrew the nut on the end of the skewer.
Once it's loose, slide the skewer out.
Each spring's narrow end faces the hub; that centres the wheel.

3.text: Lift the wheel and give it a spin.
Run your fingers round the flat band the pads touch.
You're feeling for grooves or a lip. A worn rim brakes badly and can fail.

4.text: Look at the brake from above.
Each pad should face the rim's braking track.
Check there's no debris in the brakes.

5.text: Set the wheel back between the fork blades.
The tread is moulded to roll one way. The arrow on the sidewall shows it, so point it forward.
Check the back tire the same way.

6.text: Slide the skewer back through the hub, lever on the left, away from the chain.
Thread the nut onto the other end.

7.text: Tighten the nut by hand until it's firm.
Then fold the lever closed so it lies flat along the fork, pointing up. Nothing can catch it there.

8.text: Spin the wheel and squeeze the brake. If it runs true and the pads bite, you're good to ride.
